committee_name.text: Anesthetic and Analgesic Drug Products Advisory Committee (AADPAC). (An earlier first-cycle meeting of the predecessor Anesthetic and Life Support Drugs Advisory Committee (ALSDAC) was held March 11, 2008.)

quote.quote: This application was presented to the Anesthetic and Analgesic Drug Products Advisory Committee (AADPAC) on November 6, 2015.

meeting_date.text: November 6, 2015 (approval-cycle AADPAC meeting). The first-cycle ALSDAC meeting was March 11, 2008.

quote.quote: A meeting of the Anesthetic and Analgesic Drug Products Advisory Committee was held on November 6, 2015.

recommendation.text: The committee voted 14 yes / 0 no / 0 abstain that the efficacy, safety, and overall risk-benefit profile of sugammadex support approval. Supporting votes: 13 yes / 1 no that sufficient information characterized the risk of hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis, and 14 yes / 0 no that sufficient information characterized the risk of cardiac dysrhythmias.

quote.quote: Voting to the question regarding whether the efficacy, safety and overall risk-benefit profile of sugammadex support the approval of this application resulted in 14 yes votes, with 0 no or abstain votes.

linkages.concern: The committee recommended that better characterization of the patients who appeared to be non-responders (or had a delayed/absent response to sugammadex) would be important; such patients risk prolonged paralysis.
linkages.change: FDA imposed a postmarketing requirement for the Applicant to conduct a study to determine what patient characteristics may predict a prolonged recovery, so that sugammadex administration can be avoided in those patients.

concern_quote.quote: However, they noted that it would be important to obtain information in patient populations that did not respond to the administration of sugammadex as expected.

change_quote.quote: Therefore, a postmarketing requirement will be imposed on the Applicant to conduct a study to determine what patient characteristics may predict a prolonged recovery, in which case sugammadex administration should be avoided.

linkages.concern: The committee noted it would be important to obtain safety information in patient populations not well-represented in the development program, specifically patients with significant comorbid conditions / less compensatory reserve for recovering from the hemodynamic effects of a sugammadex-related arrhythmia (ASA classification 3 and 4).
linkages.change: FDA imposed a postmarketing requirement for the Applicant to conduct a clinical trial to support a risk-benefit determination for sugammadex in patients with less compensatory reserve, such as ASA classification 3 and 4 patients.

concern_quote.quote: However, they noted it would be important to obtain safety information in certain patient populations that were not included to a significant extent in the program.

change_quote.quote: Therefore, a postmarketing requirement will be imposed on the Applicant to conduct a clinical trial is to generate data to be able to make a risk-benefit determination regarding sugammadex administration in patients who have less compensatory reserve for recovering from the hemodynamic effects of a sugammadex-related arrhythmia than those studied in the development program, such as patients categorized as being in ASA classification 3 and 4.

linkages.concern: The committee noted it would be important to obtain safety/dosing information in morbidly obese patients, a population not well-represented in the development program, given the dose-dependent risk of hypersensitivity.
linkages.change: FDA imposed a postmarketing requirement for the Applicant to conduct a clinical trial to generate data to support dosing recommendations in morbidly obese patients.

concern_quote.quote: However, they noted it would be important to obtain safety information in certain patient populations that were not included to a significant extent in the program.

change_quote.quote: Therefore, a postmarketing requirement will be imposed on the Applicant to conduct a clinical trial to generate data to support dosing recommendations in morbidly obese patients.

summary: Bridion (sugammadex) was presented to the Anesthetic and Analgesic Drug Products Advisory Committee (AADPAC) on November 6, 2015, during a later review cycle after repeated non-approval actions over hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis and cardiac dysrhythmia safety concerns. The committee voted 14-0 that the overall risk-benefit profile supported approval (13-1 on characterizing hypersensitivity risk, 14-0 on cardiac dysrhythmia risk), and the drug was approved. The committee required no additional data before approval, but recommended further study of underrepresented populations and non-responders; FDA translated these recommendations into three postmarketing requirements covering non-responder/prolonged-recovery characterization, ASA class 3-4 comorbid patients, and dosing in morbidly obese patients.
